content.title: Build Content With Hierarchy
content.hook: A page is rarely one giant paragraph. Content has relationships.
content.context:
A lesson page might look like: ```html

HTML Basics

Learn how web documents are structured.

Elements

Elements describe pieces of content.

Practice

Build a small document.

``` The headings create a visible and structural hierarchy.
goals: Use headings, paragraphs, and lists to express the hierarchy and grouping of page content.

content.question: Which element fits “Practice” when it is a section inside the page?

feedback.correct: `<h1>` names the page’s main heading. `<h2>` introduces a major section inside it.
feedback.incorrect: `<h1>` names the page’s main heading. `<h2>` introduces a major section inside it.

content.question:
You have these three lessons:

- HTML
- Page presentation
- Page behavior

When the order does not matter, which element pair represents an unordered list?

feedback.correct: Use `<ul>` for an unordered list and `<li>` for each list item.
feedback.incorrect: Use `<ul>` for an unordered list and `<li>` for each list item.

content.title: Try both list types
content.text:
Unordered list: ```html
  • HTML
  • Page structure
  • Page presentation
``` Ordered list: ```html
  1. Open the page
  2. Read the lesson
  3. Complete the exercise
``` The content is similar, but the meaning is different: one is a set, the other is a sequence.

content.question:
The product manager changes the requirement from “a list of topics” to “the steps to finish setup.”

What should change?

options.text: `<ul>` becomes `<ol>` because the order now matters.
The browser should invent the order.

feedback.correct: The element follows the meaning. When sequence matters, an ordered list communicates that relationship.
feedback.incorrect: The element follows the meaning. When sequence matters, an ordered list communicates that relationship.

content.title: Build a small outline
content.text:
Create: ```html

Forge Academy

Build practical frontend engineering skill.

What you will learn

  • HTML structure
  • Page presentation
  • Page behavior
``` **Task:** Add a new section called “How to start” with three ordered steps: 1. Open the lesson. 2. Predict the result. 3. Build the solution.

content.question:
Which structure best represents this requirement?

“First choose a lesson, then complete the practice, then explain your answer.”

options.text: An ordered list with three list items
An unordered list with three list items

feedback.correct: The requirement expresses a sequence, so the document should express a sequence too.
feedback.incorrect: The requirement expresses a sequence, so the document should express a sequence too.
